about: What Lunenburg’s school buses cost, by year since FY2010: the school day against athletics, budgeted and spent; athletics by sport; and what the Dee Bus contract fixes through FY2028.

circuit_breaker.comment: Supplemental payment increased transport reimbursement to 75%.

conclusions.basis: General fund school accounts, voted budget and spent at the close (expended plus still committed): MUNIS year-end reports FY2023 to FY2026, the Finance Committee’s ledger history before that. Which account is which kind is ours, by function and object code.
conclusions.claim: Athletic buses were 6.4% of school transportation spending in FY2026.
conclusions.detail: In FY2026 the general fund spent $976,500 on regular routes, $633,291 on special education transportation, $110,650 on athletic buses and $3,902 on band trips — $1,724,343 in all. On the budget side alone, athletics was 7.7% of what was voted. From FY2010 to FY2026 athletics never passed 6.4% of what was spent, and fell as low as 1.8% in FY2013.
conclusions.not_shown: Athletic buses the athletic fee fund paid for are not in the general fund and not in this share: in FY2024 the district’s own sheet put athletic transportation at about three times the general fund line. Every line is net of whatever else pays for it (rule 11).
conclusions.so_what: The school-day buses — regular routes and special education vans — were 93.4%; band trips the rest.

conclusions.basis: The district’s sport-by-sport workbook (records request, June 2026), row sums; the general fund athletic transportation account in the MUNIS year-end reports; the district’s FY2026 budget overview.
conclusions.claim: The district’s own sheet put FY2024 athletic bus costs at $117,555; the voted line was $40,000.
conclusions.detail: The district’s sport-by-sport workbook, hand-assembled and received by records request, totals $117,555 for FY2024 and $91,066 for FY2025. The general fund line was voted at $40,000 in both years and spent $40,000 and $87,822. The district’s FY2026 overview says the line was “budgeted to cover full cost of transportation for athletics; athletic revolving can not support these increased costs”.
conclusions.not_shown: The workbook is assembled by hand and a second district sheet gives different figures for several of the same sports. Nothing published says how many trips either year ran, so a change in trips and a change in who paid cannot be fully separated.

see.label: The athletics fee fund, line by line

conclusions.so_what: So the line’s jump to $127,550 in FY2026 moved who pays, as the district said; the cost was already there.

conclusions.basis: OUR ESTIMATE. Dollars from the district’s sport-by-sport workbook (stated), divided by a trip priced from the Dee Bus bid form’s FY2026 rates and its own estimate of 100 trips, 6,500 miles and four hours of waiting per trip.
conclusions.claim: Our estimate: FY2025 athletic bus spending equals about 97 trips at the new contract’s prices.
conclusions.detail: The sheet’s FY2025 transportation, $91,066, divided by the cost of the bid form’s own average trip at FY2026 prices: 65 miles at $6.50 a mile and 4 hours of waiting at $130.00 an hour, $942.50. With no waiting time a trip is $422.50 and the same dollars are about 216 trips. FY2025 prices are not held; if they were lower, the counts are higher.
conclusions.not_shown: Nobody publishes a trip count. A sport that rides farther, or waits longer, buys fewer trips for the same dollars; golf and cross country may ride short buses. The FY2025 dollars were paid under the previous contract, whose rates were requested and not delivered.
conclusions.so_what: Girls Soccer buses cost the most, about 8 trips; football next. No sport topped $7,850.

conclusions.basis: The Dee Bus bid form (Exhibit E), signed 27 December 2024, every rate checked against its printed totals; the agreement’s term; the district’s FY2027 budget book.
conclusions.claim: The bus contract already fixes FY2028’s regular-route price: $1,131,390 for 11 buses.
conclusions.detail: Prices per bus per day are bid for every year: $485 and $515 in FY2026 rising to $565 and $588.50 in FY2028, for 8 77-passenger and 3 83-passenger buses, 180 days. The FY2027 budget carries $1,053,360 for the line, the contract’s second-year price to the dollar. The option years are priced at $1,189,800 and $1,284,984.
conclusions.not_shown: The contract prices regular routes; it does not fix how many buses run — the form lets the district add or drop up to two a year at the same unit prices. The contract’s price is not what the town will pay: the line is voted net of anything else that pays for it.
conclusions.so_what: A known 7.4% rise. It ends June 2028; renewal, or the two priced option years, is the decision.

conclusions.basis: The district’s FY2026 budget overview (“Dee Bus 7.6% line increase = $69,300”); the contract’s FY2026 prices; the FY2025 general education transportation budget, budget to budget.
conclusions.claim: FY2026’s 7.6% bus increase is the new contract’s first-year price over the old budget line.
conclusions.detail: The contract’s FY2026 regular-route price is $976,500; the FY2025 line was $907,200; the difference is $69,300. If the old line paid for the same 11 buses it averaged $458.18 a bus a day against $493.18 now, and all of the rise is price. If it paid for 10, it averaged $504.00 and the rise is a bus.
conclusions.not_shown: The FY2025 rates and fleet were requested and not delivered. A district presentation says eleven buses were in use; that is a statement, not a rate.
conclusions.so_what: Whether it bought a price rise or an extra bus cannot be told without the old contract.

conclusions.basis: General fund special education transportation account, voted against spent at the close; DESE’s circuit breaker schedule, transportation column; the district’s FY2026 budget overview.
conclusions.claim: Special education transportation spending rose from $322,047 in FY2019 to $633,291 in FY2026.
conclusions.detail: FY2019 is the base because it is the last year before the 2020 school closures — our choice. The line came in under budget every year from FY2016 to FY2023. Overruns: $65,455 over in FY2024; $67,557 over in FY2026. The state’s circuit breaker paid back $111,560 for out-of-district transportation in FY2025 and $94,993 in FY2026 — never netted here, and it covers only children placed outside the district. The district’s FY2026 overview gives the line’s rise as a 7% rate increase and more vans and monitors.
conclusions.not_shown: The van contract is not in the archive, so how much of the rise is price, routes, children or monitors cannot be split. The cause given is the district’s; nothing here tests it.
conclusions.so_what: It ran over its voted budget in FY2024 and FY2026; the district cites more vans and monitors.

conclusions.basis: MUNIS FY2026 year-end report, account 535025, original appropriation and transfers; the contract’s FY2026 price; Finance Committee minutes, 20 March 2025; MUNIS fund 1308 account 437601.
conclusions.claim: The FY2026 bus line was voted $11,000 under the contract price, then topped back up mid-year.
conclusions.detail: Voted $965,500; contract price $976,500; transfers of $11,000 during the year brought the line to $976,500, all of it spent. Where the fee receipts landed is not stated anywhere; an account named SCH. CHOICE BUS FEE in the school choice fund took in $50,628.44 in FY2025 and $52,717.04 in FY2026, after nothing in FY2023 and FY2024.
conclusions.not_shown: That the fund 1308 receipts are the bus fees is a hypothesis: the account is named for school choice, and nothing published ties it to the fee. The number of families who paid is not published.
conclusions.so_what: The Finance Committee was told the bus fee cut the line by that much; where the fees are booked is unstated.

conclusions.basis: The district’s FY2027 budget book, balanced and level-service scenarios; School Committee minutes, 26 August 2026, as minuted; the contract’s FY2027 rates for our trip estimate.
conclusions.claim: FY2027’s budget cut athletic buses to $0; restoring high school buses was put at $58,880.
conclusions.detail: The balanced budget carried $0; the FY2027 level-service budget had carried $127,550. The Superintendent told the School Committee on 26 August 2026 the lower figure came from scheduling competitions closer to Lunenburg, more home games and actual schedules. At FY2027 contract prices $58,880 is about 59 of the bid form’s average trips — our estimate.
conclusions.not_shown: The $58,880 is the Superintendent’s figure as minuted, not a contract or a ledger amount, and whether Special Town Meeting funded it is not in this archive’s ledgers yet. Middle school buses are not in it.
conclusions.so_what: The August plan: $10,000 from the town and $50,000 from the athletics fee fund.

said.quote: it is a 3 year contract with tentative increases over the 3 years
said.why: The district bringing the Dee Bus bid to the Committee, before the contract was signed in May 2025.

said.quote: 7.6% increase in Dee Bus services 7% increase in vanpool for special education transportation
said.why: How the FY2026 increase was described to the Finance Committee: a percentage, with no fleet or rate beside it.

said.quote: The cost of athletic transportation is not up 200%. The way we are accounting for athletic transportation has been corrected from past practice that was done incorrectly.
said.why: A School Committee member’s explanation of the FY2026 athletic line. The by-sport workbook is consistent with it: the cost was already about three times the line in FY2024.

said.quote: The implementation of transportation fee reduced the student transportation line by $11,000.
said.why: The only statement in the record of how the new bus fee entered the budget. It is the same amount the FY2026 line was voted below the contract price.

said.quote: A fourth transfer to move funds to the athletic transportation, special detail, dues and fees and the high school after school stipends, this is the first phase move making monies available in the athletic portion of the budget. We can go back and reclassify expenses that had been charged against the revolving account.
said.why: The FY2025 transfer that took the athletic transportation line from its voted amount to what it spent: costs charged to the fee fund, moved onto the town line.

said.quote: We have received 1,074 bus requests, and have 494 unpaid at this time.
said.why: The only count of riders in the record, taken before the first fee year began. A request is not a rider and an unpaid request is not a refusal.

said.quote: Chris Menard asks for a copy of the bus contracts. The schools will be going out to bid for school buses in January.
said.why: Said in FY2024, the year the regular-route line ran furthest over its budget, and ten months before the bid this page reads.

said.quote: Chris Menard suggests the schools work on the contract as it is scheduled to be renewed in 2028.
said.why: A Finance Committee member pointing at the one transportation decision the town controls on a schedule: the contract ends on 30 June 2028.

said.quote: We will need to pay Dee Bus Company upfront and that cost is $731.50.
said.why: One trip, priced under the new contract: a class field trip. It sits inside the range this page’s per-trip estimate uses.

said.quote: All athletic transportation would be cut saving: $127,550.
said.why: The FY2027 balanced budget, as presented to the Finance Committee.

said.quote: The transportation for Middle-High Band would be reduced to $5,000.
said.why: The same presentation. The FY2027 balanced budget in the district’s book carries nothing for either band transportation line; the minute and the book differ, and the record here does not say which held.

said.quote: a more creative avenue for further conversation needs to be had about the athletic transportation
said.why: A parent at public comment, on the cut. The same meeting heard a student ask why teachers were being cut while athletic transportation was not yet.

said.quote: two buses will be necessary for transportation to away games
said.why: The football boosters, offering to pay for buses after the FY2027 cut.

said.quote: the private transportation waiver currently included in FinalForms, which allowed student-athletes to be transported privately while district transportation was unavailable
said.why: A parent’s question: with district buses cut, athletes were being driven privately under a signed waiver. The FY2026 athletic line had come in under its revised budget.

said.quote: the verified transportation cost was approximately $58,880, which she rounded to $60,000. Of that amount, $10,000 would come from the additional appropriation and $50,000 from the athletic revolving account.
said.why: The Superintendent’s plan to restore high school athletic buses for FY2027. She attributed the lower figure to scheduling competitions closer to Lunenburg, more home competitions, and estimating from actual schedules.

said.quote: 75% reimbursement for FY25 out of district special education transportation costs through the circuit breaker program increased from 44%
said.why: The district’s account of the state’s change to the transportation half of the circuit breaker. The state’s own schedule shows the payment rising the same year.
